::: {#sol-absorption}

**$A \cup (A \cap B) \subseteq A$.**
Let $x \in A \cup (A \cap B)$.
Then $x \in A$ or $x \in A \cap B$.
In the first case, $x \in A$.
In the second case, $x \in A$ and $x \in B$, so again $x \in A$.
Either way, $x \in A$ (@def-proof-by-cases).

**$A \subseteq A \cup (A \cap B)$.**
Let $x \in A$.
Then "$x \in A$ or $x \in A \cap B$" is true,
since its first part is true (@def-or),
so $x \in A \cup (A \cap B)$.

Each side is a subset of the other,
so an element is in one side exactly when it is in the other,
and the two sets are equal (@def-set).

:::
